en.t: So it really is a monster after all.
I want to paint this kind of monster picture too.

units.source_text: 對人類極度恐懼的人，反而更希望見識一下可怕的妖怪心理，

en.t: People who are terrified of human beings to an extreme degree instead come to want to glimpse the psychology of frightening monsters,

units.source_text: 與越是神經質的膽怯之人，越是祈望暴風雨來得更猛烈的心理如出一轍。

en.t: just like the psychology by which the more nervous and timid a person is, the more fiercely they pray for the storm to rage.

units.source_text: 啊，這群畫家深受人類這種妖怪的傷害和恫嚇，

en.t: Ah, this group of painters had been deeply wounded and intimidated by the monster called humanity,

units.source_text: 最終相信幻影，在光天化日的自然中，活靈活現地目睹了妖怪。

en.t: until at last they believed in phantoms and vividly saw monsters in nature under broad daylight.

units.source_text: 但他們從不搞笑，以此來掩飾妖怪，而是竭力表現出自己所見的景物。

en.t: But they never used clowning to cover up the monsters; instead, they strove to express the scenes exactly as they had seen them.

units.source_text: 正如竹一所言，毅然畫出「妖怪的畫像」。

en.t: Just as Takeichi said, they resolutely painted portraits of monsters.

units.source_text: 一想到我未來的夥伴就在這裡，不禁興奮得熱淚奪眶而出。

en.t: When I thought that my future companions were here, I became so excited that hot tears sprang to my eyes.
